name: odds-api
description:
The Odds API V1 provides sports and racing events, bookmaker odds, exchange and prediction-market order books,
live price updates, betting opportunity snapshots, and result lookups for production integrations.

Authenticate every request with `X-API-Key: <your_api_key>` unless an endpoint explicitly states it is public.
Use `https://api.odds-api.net/v1` as the production base URL.

Snapshot endpoints return JSON and include timestamps or resume tokens when live updates are available.
`/stream` endpoints use Server-Sent Events (`text/event-stream`) and `/ws` endpoints use WebSockets. Stream
messages use the same shape in both transports: an event name such as `delta`, `heartbeat`, or `resync`, plus a
JSON payload. Store the latest `resume` value and pass it back as `since` after reconnecting.

Production clients should start with catalog discovery, page event lists with `limit` and `cursor`, fetch odds
snapshots for initial state, then use streams for hot events. Recommended starting polling intervals are:
catalog metadata every 6-24 hours, sports event lists every 5-15 minutes, racing event lists every 1-5 minutes,
odds snapshots every 60-120 seconds when streams are not used, betting opportunity snapshots every 30-120 seconds,
and results every 1-5 minutes after the event starts until settled.

Handle HTTP 429 by honoring `Retry-After` when present, otherwise use jittered exponential backoff. Use
`/usage` to detect monthly API-credit quota exhaustion and `/limits` to discover response, stream, add-on, and
plan caps. Most standard API calls use 1 credit; large odds snapshots, history, broad aggregate feeds, and
support-approved betting feeds may use multiple credits as weighted metering rolls out. Cache snapshots by request
shape, respect `ttl_seconds` when present, display `as_of_ts_ms`, and use `bookmaker_as_of_ts_ms` when a
per-bookmaker freshness decision matters. `target_refresh_interval_seconds` is a scheduling target, not an
artificial plan delay or a guarantee that an upstream bookmaker answered on time. Keep the most recent `resume` token with
cached state. On stream disconnect, reconnect with `since=<last_resume>` and `catchup=true`; on `resync`, reload
the snapshot before applying more deltas.

Odds can change quickly. Check event and bookmaker freshness timestamps, handle empty arrays, suspended selections, rate limits, and stale
prices before displaying or acting on any betting data.

New odds-api.net API keys default to a compact response shape that keeps essential IDs, prices, teams, markets,
timestamps, and resume tokens while omitting raw payloads, source metadata, internal/debug IDs, bookmaker links,
and non-offered price columns. Existing API keys keep the historical full response shape unless they explicitly
pass the compacting query flags. There is no public `profile` parameter; use the documented per-field flags when
you need to opt a compact client back into a specific field group.
